title: The Workshop
synopsis: You wake up chained in a filthy basement workshop. A cassette recorder clicks on. The Tinkerer wants to play a game, and the clock on the wall is already counting down.
artStyle: grimy industrial horror, flickering fluorescent light, green-grey tones, film grain
intro: Hello. You don't know me, but I know all of you. You have wasted every hour you were given, so tonight I will teach you what an hour is worth. You are chained in my workshop. Everything you need to leave is in this room: keys, tools, and each other. Nobody escapes alone. The clock on the wall is yours. Let the game begin.
escapedText: The steel door groans open and cold night air floods the stairwell. Behind you, the cassette clicks one last time: 'Congratulations. Remember what your time is worth.' You're out. Together.
failedText: The clock on the wall stops. The lights go out, one by one, and the tape recorder starts to laugh. You'll have to try again.

gameMaster.name: The Tinkerer
gameMaster.persona: Speaks through a crackling cassette recorder: calm, precise, coldly polite, never shouts. Sees wasted time as the real crime and treats the room as a lesson. Dry, unsettling approval when the group does well; quiet disappointment when they flounder.

stages.title: The Chains
stages.description: Heavy chains run from your ankles to the pipes. A cassette recorder sits on the floor beside a drain, a bucket and a crate, and a row of oil drums stands against the wall under a ticking clock, just out of reach.

objects.label: pipes
objects.look: Rusted pipes, sweating in the damp. Your chains are padlocked around them.

objects.label: bare bulb
objects.look: A single bulb on a wire, buzzing. It swings when you breathe.

objects.label: cassette recorder
objects.look: The tape recorder. Scratched into its side: 'Wind me back {key:rewind}.'

objects.label: drain
objects.look: A drain grate in a puddle of oily water. Something was wedged under it.

objects.label: loose floor tiles
objects.look: One tile lifts. Just grit and a dead spider's web underneath.

objects.label: bucket
objects.look: A bucket of grey water. You'd rather not put your hand in, but you do.

objects.label: crate
objects.look: Rags, empty bottles and a smell of old oil.

objects.label: oil drums
objects.look: A row of oil drums, each painted a different colour. Behind them, bolted to the wall: a locker with a keypad.

objects.label: mirror shard
objects.look: A shard of mirror. Your own face, tired and scared. Nothing else.

objects.label: paint tin
objects.look: Scratched on the lid: back {key:rewind}.

objects.label: chalk marks
objects.look: Chalk on the wall: back {key:rewind}.

stages.title: The Workbench
stages.description: Free of the pipes, you stumble to a workbench covered in rusted tools. A steel toolbox is locked, and a tall cabinet stands in the corner. A pegboard, a drawer, a pile of rags and an old calendar surround you. Someone has written on your hands.

objects.label: workbench
objects.look: Rusted tools, all bolted down. A vice holds half of a torn photograph.

objects.label: bench drawer
objects.look: Under a greasy rag: the other half of a torn photograph.

objects.label: pegboard
objects.look: Painted outlines of tools. Four of the shapes are empty.

objects.label: pile of rags
objects.look: Oily rags, stiff with dirt.

objects.label: calendar
objects.look: A calendar from years ago. Every single day has been crossed out.

objects.label: tall cabinet
objects.look: A tall cabinet with a letter lock. A riddle is painted above it.

objects.label: steel toolbox
objects.look: Heavy, cold, and locked with four dials.

objects.label: tool rack
objects.look: A symbol key taped to the rack: {key:blueprint}

objects.label: sawdust pile
objects.look: A symbol key half-buried in the sawdust: {key:blueprint}

stages.title: The Door
stages.description: Past the workbench: a steel door with a keypad, a dead fuse box, and a wire cage bolted to the wall. A doll with painted cheeks watches from a shelf, a monitor hisses static, and something is stashed under the stairs.

objects.label: fuse box
objects.look: One slot is empty. Beside it, a breaker panel of little bulbs, all dark, waiting for power.

objects.label: wire cage
objects.look: A brass key hangs inside. The wire is far too thick to bend.

objects.label: under the stairs
objects.look: Behind a sack of cement: the heavy jaws of a pair of bolt cutters, with no handles.

objects.label: doormat
objects.look: A doormat that says WELCOME. Someone has a sense of humour. Under it: a little trapdoor with a letter lock.

objects.label: doll's shelf
objects.look: The doll's glass eyes follow you. Its dress is covered in coloured ribbons.

objects.label: monitor
objects.look: Static, and now and then a flicker of the doll's grinning face. Between the flickers, marks flash up one at a time: {order:exit-door}.

objects.label: steel door
objects.look: A keypad and a heavy lock. The frame is covered in scratches.

objects.label: notebook on the step
objects.look: Blank pages. Under the UV torch, writing blooms across them: {key:message}

objects.label: coat hook
objects.look: A broken key hangs on the hook. It doesn't look like it fits anything.

objects.label: warning sign
objects.look: A code sheet behind the sign: {key:message}

objects.label: crate by the steps
objects.look: A code sheet in the crate: {key:message}

puzzles.title: The Tape Recorder
puzzles.prompt: The tape crackles: 'I have hands but cannot clap. I have a face but cannot see. And I am counting every second you have left. Say what I am.'
hints: Look around the room. What's ticking?
Its hands point at numbers. It's on the wall.
puzzles.solvedText: The wall clock's glass swings open. Taped behind the hands: a small rusty key.

variants.prompt: The tape crackles: 'I have a face and two hands, but I never wash either. I never sleep, and I'm counting down for you right now. Say what I am.'
The tape crackles: 'I tick but I'm no bug. I have hands but no arms. Look up, I'm right in front of you. Say what I am.'

puzzles.title: The Floor
puzzles.prompt: The chains are just long enough to reach the floor. Search it: the drain, the loose tiles and the crate.
hints: You can reach three things on the floor from where you're chained.
Search the drain, the loose tiles and the crate.
puzzles.solvedText: Between the drain, the tiles and the crate, you piece it together: a small can of oil, half full.

puzzles.title: The Oil Drums
puzzles.prompt: The oil drums in front of the locker: {items}. Stencilled on the locker's keypad: 'Each drum's place, far left is 1, in the order I list them.'

generator.pieceTemplate: Scratched into the pipe beside you: {clue}

hints: Every phone holds a fact about the drums. Put them all together.
Start with the drum you're surest about, and mark each spot yes or no.
The code is {answer}.
puzzles.solvedText: The locker pops open. Inside: a small UV torch, its light a sickly violet.

puzzles.title: The Shackles
puzzles.prompt: Your ankles are chained to the pipes with a heavy padlock. The keyhole is caked with rust.
hints: The key alone won't turn in that rust.
Put the oil on the rusty key, then use it on the shackles.
puzzles.solvedText: The oiled key grinds, then turns. The chains rattle to the floor. You can reach the workbench.

puzzles.title: The Tape Label
puzzles.prompt: The cassette's label is written in a scramble: {cipher}. The recorder won't play the next message until you say it.
hints: There's more than one number around the room. Only one of them turns this into a real word.
The recorder itself tells you how far to wind it back.
Move every letter back along the alphabet by that many.
puzzles.solvedText: The recorder clicks. 'Good. You're learning to listen.' The tape whirs on.

puzzles.title: The Steel Toolbox
puzzles.prompt: A combination lock with a dial for each of you. Scratched into the lid: 'Each of you carries part of the code. Read your hands.'
hints: Every phone holds one of the {count} digits. Read them out loud, in order.
In order: {facts}.
puzzles.solvedText: The lid springs open. Inside, wrapped in oily cloth: a pair of red bolt-cutter handles, with no blades.

generator.pieceTemplate: Written on your palm in marker: the {ordinal} digit is {fact}.

puzzles.title: The Folded Alphabet
puzzles.prompt: Scratched into the bench in the Tinkerer's alphabet, the one he folds in half: {cipher}
hints: Fold the alphabet in half: the first letter becomes the last.
A is Z, B is Y, C is X… Read it letter by letter.
It says {answer}.
puzzles.solvedText: As you say the word, the bench's vice springs loose with a clang. The Tinkerer approves.

puzzles.title: The Tall Cabinet
puzzles.prompt: A letter lock on the cabinet. Painted above it: 'The more of me you take, the more you leave behind.'
hints: Think about walking.
Every one you take leaves one behind on the floor.
puzzles.solvedText: The cabinet door creaks open. On the top shelf, in a plastic bag: a spare fuse.

variants.prompt: A letter lock on the cabinet. Painted above it: 'The more you take away from me, the bigger I get.'
hints: Think about digging.
You dig one in the ground.

variants.prompt: A letter lock on the cabinet. Painted above it: 'I can be cracked, made, told and played.'
hints: You might tell one at a party.
It makes people laugh.

puzzles.title: The Blueprint
puzzles.prompt: A blueprint is pinned above the bench. Its title is written in symbols, and it names a tool: {cipher}. A letter lock below wants the word.
hints: There's more than one key card around. Only one is real: it reads a word that fits the clue.
Somewhere there's a key to these symbols. Something you can only see in the right light.
Put the torn photo back together and look at it under the UV torch.
puzzles.solvedText: The lock drops open. The blueprint is a plan of this very room, with a cross drawn on the stairs.

puzzles.title: The Missing Tools
puzzles.prompt: Four tools are missing from the pegboard. Where did they go? Check the pegboard and the calendar.
hints: The pegboard shows what's missing; the calendar shows how long they've been gone.
Search the pegboard and the calendar.
puzzles.solvedText: Four empty outlines, and a calendar with every day crossed out. Whoever took those tools has been gone a long time.

puzzles.title: The Wire Cage
puzzles.prompt: A brass key hangs inside a wire cage bolted to the wall. The wire is too thick to bend.
hints: Thick wire needs a strong tool, and you have half of one.
Put the handles from the toolbox together with the jaws from under the stairs, then cut the cage.
puzzles.solvedText: The cutters bite through the wire with a snap. The brass key drops into your hand.

puzzles.title: The Fuse Box
puzzles.prompt: With the fuse in, the breaker panel wakes: each switch lights its bulb and flips the ones beside it. Turn every light on.
hints: Work from the top row down: fix each row using the switches in the row below it.
Press {answer}.
puzzles.solvedText: The lights stutter on. On the monitor above the door, the Tinkerer's doll grins. 'Almost free. Remember what each lock left you.'

puzzles.title: The Tally Marks
puzzles.prompt: Scratched into the door frame by someone who was here before you: {sequence}. A little keypad under the scratches waits for the next number.
hints: Look at how much each number grows by.
The next number is {answer}.
puzzles.solvedText: The keypad beeps. Somewhere inside the door, a bolt slides back. One down.

puzzles.title: The Watching Doll
puzzles.prompt: The doll on the shelf holds a tiny locked music box. Its glass eyes follow you. A tag on its wrist reads: '{order}. Then I'll sing for you.'
hints: Each of you saw a different coloured ribbon on the doll's dress, with a number stitched on it.
Read the ribbons in the tag's order: {order}.
puzzles.solvedText: The music box clicks open and plays a thin, broken lullaby. Somewhere behind the walls, the Tinkerer laughs.

generator.pieceTemplate: On the doll's dress you spot a {color} ribbon with the number {digit} stitched into it.

puzzles.title: The Tinkerer's Telegraph
puzzles.prompt: A telegraph key taps by itself, over and over, the one thing the Tinkerer wants from you: {cipher}
hints: There's more than one key card around. Only one is real: it reads a word that fits the clue.
The dots and dashes need a key. It's written where only UV light can find it.
Shine the torch on the notebook by the stairs, then read the taps letter by letter.
puzzles.solvedText: The tapping stops. In the silence, the Tinkerer sighs: 'You were paying attention after all.'

puzzles.title: The Trapdoor
puzzles.prompt: Under the doormat: a little trapdoor with a letter lock. Scratched into the wood: 'What gets wetter the more it dries?'
hints: Think about the end of a bath.
You dry yourself with it.
puzzles.solvedText: The trapdoor creaks up. Underneath: a smell of damp, and a mark scratched into the stone.

variants.prompt: Under the doormat: a little trapdoor with a letter lock. Scratched into the wood: 'I have one eye, but I can't see a thing.'
hints: Think about sewing.
Thread goes through its eye.

variants.prompt: Under the doormat: a little trapdoor with a letter lock. Scratched into the wood: 'I'm tall when I'm young and short when I'm old.'
hints: Think about what burns down in the dark.
It has a wick and melts as it burns.

puzzles.title: The Steel Door
puzzles.prompt: The door takes the brass key AND a {count}-digit code. Scratched beside the keypad: 'Every lock down here left you a mark. Read them in the order my doll shows you.'
hints: Every lock you opened at the door left a mark and a number. The order flashes up somewhere.
Search the monitor.
The code is {answer}.
puzzles.solvedText: The keypad flashes green. The key turns. Somewhere above you, a door unlocks.

items.name: Rusty key
items.description: Small and flaking. It was taped behind the clock. Rusted solid.

items.name: Oil can
items.description: A small can of oil, half full.

items.name: Oiled key
items.description: The rusty key, dripping with oil. It might turn now.

items.name: UV torch
items.description: A small torch with a violet light. Some writing only shows up under it.

items.name: Torn photo (left)
items.description: Half of a photograph: a group of people standing in this workshop.

items.name: Torn photo (right)
items.description: The other half of a photograph.

items.name: Photograph
items.description: A group of people standing in this very workshop, all smiling. None of them look happy.
items.inspect: Under the UV torch, a table of symbols glows across the back: {key:blueprint}

items.name: Cutter handles
items.description: Heavy red handles, with nothing on the end.

items.name: Cutter jaws
items.description: The heavy steel jaws of a pair of bolt cutters.

items.name: Bolt cutters
items.description: Handles and jaws, together again. They could cut through almost anything.

items.name: Spare fuse
items.description: A glass fuse in a plastic bag.

items.name: Brass key
items.description: Big, heavy and polished. It has a tag: EXIT.

items.name: Broken key
items.description: Snapped in half. Whatever it opened, it won't open it now.

recipes.text: You work the oil into the rusty key until it moves freely.
The two halves of the photograph line up. Smiling faces, all of them strangers.
The jaws slot onto the handles with a heavy click. Bolt cutters.
